stories.title: Mixture analysis of urinary parabens and their associations with reproductive hormones in iranian women
stories.description: While parabens are widely used, concerns exist regarding their potential to impair reproductive health through endocrine disruption. However, evidence on impacts of paraben mixtures remains insufficient, particularly regarding hormonal regulation in women. We conducted a cross-sectional study of 84 women of reproductive age (18–45 years) at Imam Reza Hospital, Kermanshah. Urinary concentrations of methylparaben (MePB), ethylparaben (EtPB), propylparaben (PrPB), and butylparaben (BuPB) were quantified via GC-MS and adjusted for specific gravity, while serum levels of follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), luteinizing hormone (LH), and prolactin were measured using ELISA. We employed multivariable linear regression and exploratory relative-weight analysis to evaluate mixture-based associations, supplemented by non-carcinogenic risk assessment. MePB was most abundant, whereas BuPB accounted for 65.1% of cumulative estrogenic activity (EEQ). Mixture models revealed significant associations exclusively with LH (n = 35), with PrPB (45%, p = 0.021) and EtPB (24%, p = 0.032) showing positive contributions, and BuPB (23%, p = 0.033) and MePB (8%, p = 0.037) showing inverse contributions; no significant associations were observed for FSH or prolactin. Although hazard quotients remained below 1 (95th percentile HI = 0.0998) and Monte Carlo simulations confirmed negligible non-carcinogenic risk, paraben mixtures may be related to hormonal levels. These findings highlight the subtle endocrine-disrupting potential of parabens at these levels.

stories.title: Association of cumulative TCBI exposure with incident stroke in cardiovascular kidney metabolic syndrome stages 0 to 3
stories.description: Stroke continues to impose a substantial global health burden, particularly among individuals with cardiovascular–kidney–metabolic (CKM) syndrome. Single measurements may not fully reflect metabolic exposure over time. This investigation assessed the associations of cumulative TCBI exposure and two-time-point TCBI patterns with incident stroke among individuals with CKM stages 0–3. This study sought to evaluate how cumulative and temporal changes in the TCBI relate to stroke occurrence across CKM stages by analyzing 4475 CHARLS participants aged 45 years or older, assessing TCBI at two occasions, categorizing longitudinal pattern via K-means clustering, and employing multivariable logistic regression combined with restricted cubic spline modeling. Higher cumulative TCBI (CumTCBI) and membership in the high-level two-time-point pattern group were associated with greater odds of incident stroke. In the fully adjusted model, each 1-unit increase in CumTCBI was associated with 12% higher odds (OR = 1.12, 95% CI 1.07–1.17). The corresponding OR for the high-level versus low-level pattern group was 1.66 (95% CI 1.32–2.08). The association was nonlinear, with an exploratory change point near 27.83, and remained directionally consistent in sensitivity analyses. Higher CumTCBI and high-level two-time-point TCBI patterns were associated with incident stroke among middle-aged and older adults classified as CKM stages 0–3. These findings represent epidemiological associations and do not establish the clinical utility of TCBI for individual risk stratification.

stories.title: Botune: an AI-supported scaffolding system for children’s drawing-based narrative expression in nature learning
stories.description: Nature exploration fosters children’s cognitive development and environmental awareness; however, kindergarten curricula are often constrained by limited resources and repetitive interaction, leaving children’s observations only weakly integrated into structured understanding and expression. We present Botune, an AI-supported creative-expression tool for kindergarten planting activities that integrates plant observation, drawing, spoken narration, and animation-based sharing. We conducted an exploratory, fixed-order within-participant study in kindergarten planting classes with 27 children and three educators; 24 complete cases were analysed after excluding data from three children who did not complete the drawing task. The traditional activity preceded the Botune-supported activity by seven days. The proportion of activity time spent observing and teacher-rated involvement scores during sharing were higher in the later session. The later narrations contained significantly more actions and character interactions; character counts were descriptively higher but did not remain statistically significant after Holm correction, and state- or emotion-related expressions did not differ significantly. These semantic counts index narrative elaboration rather than overall narrative quality or general narrative ability. These differences cannot be attributed to Botune alone. Scientific knowledge and conceptual understanding were not directly assessed by these measures. The study offers exploratory observations and design considerations for AI-supported narrative expression in kindergarten nature learning.

stories.title: Delivery of transgenes into Gαo-rich subcortical structures of the mouse brain with potential applications for GNAO1 encephalopathy
stories.description: Adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors are widely used for transgene delivery into the mouse brain in preclinical studies, yet AAV methodology requires customization for each neurological disease. In this study, we aimed to identify the optimal approach for AAV-mediated transduction of brain regions with high expression of GNAO1, which encodes the signaling protein Gαo. Mutations in GNAO1 cause the neurodevelopmental disorder GNAO1 encephalopathy. Using whole-brain confocal imaging, we identified the highest density of Gαo-positive neuronal somata in the striatum, thalamus, cerebellar Purkinje cell layer, and pyramidal layer of the hippocampal CA2 field in the adult mouse brain. We compared intracerebroventricular and intravenous administration of neurotropic AAVs expressing fluorescent reporters in wild-type mice. Intracerebroventricular injection into neonatal mice resulted in poor penetration into deep Gαo-rich brain regions. In contrast, retro-orbital administration of AAV9 in adult mice led to uniform vector distribution across Gαo-positive cortical and subcortical regions. For the AAV9 variant Y446F/Y731F, we demonstrated transgene delivery into neurons of dopaminergic and GABAergic pathways involved in Gαo signaling, with low tropism to GFAP-positive cells. Finally, we used AAV9-Y446F/Y731F to deliver a dual-function vector designed to silence endogenous Gnao1 and express a replacement GNAO1 transgene. Although in vitro testing was successful and brain delivery met expectations, transgene expression remained low, indicating the need for expression cassette improvement. Together, our findings define an effective AAV strategy for targeting Gαo-rich regions of the mouse brain and support development of gene therapy for GNAO1 encephalopathy.
